Hub design follows the benchmark's two-track rule: /guides/ offers exactly two choices (Use an app / Build an app), and /use/ has a 'Something went wrong?' block linking to troubleshooting. Pager order inside the Use track is install > open > notebook usage > troubleshooting, which is task order.

gaps.requirement: Benchmark 7 and priority 5: 'Guide completeness 100% of critical guides have prerequisites, expected result, failure route' via an automated content checklist; broken links via build-time validation; test documentation as part of release; findability measured
gaps.current: Automated today: dead internal links and anchors, unique meta descriptions, one h1, heading order, generic link text and image alt (check_site.py and check_design.py, both 0 problems). Not automated, and the 0-problem result proves it: (1) guide completeness. No script or data/guides.yaml field marks a guide as critical or checks its headings. My heuristic checklist found 15 critical guides missing most of the four components (G3), yet the build is green. (2) The literal Markdown link text on /guides/template-synchronization/ (G3) passes check_site because it is not an <a>. (3) Search outcomes. Nothing asserts that 'Windows protected your PC' still reaches install#windows, and the 4 failing benchmark queries in G2 are invisible to the build. (4) Typos. 'finnisehd', 'LabConstrisctor' (notebook-usage), 'bellow' (initialise-repository, installer guides) and 'intialisation' (code-hiding) are not caught. (5) The `notebook-usage` link 'this guide' for 'How to Run Notebooks?' points to a BUILD guide (../code-hiding/) and the 'this guide' text only passes because DESIGN rules apply to hand-written pages, while KNOWN_EXCEPTIONS lists only one entry. Cannot be automated and needs real testers: first-time completion >=4 of 5 testers; the ~15 minute first analysis (clean install plus data); each platform route (Windows, macOS Intel/Apple Silicon, Linux); scientific reproducibility on pinned data; keyboard and screen-reader checks beyond axe-type scans; whether 'Check that it worked' texts match the real UI. I did not run any of these on a real OS or with human testers.
gaps.proposal: Site repo. (a) Add scripts/check_guides.py (kept under 300 lines, one function per rule). It reads a new `critical:` list in data/guides.yaml and, for each listed guide, fails the build unless the rendered article has headings matching the four required components (prerequisites / check that it worked / if it fails / next), a time statement where marked, and at least one image with alt for steps flagged `screens: true`; it names the guide and the missing part, with no fallback. (b) Extend check_site.py to fail on '](' or '[x](' text inside <main> outside code blocks. (c) Add data/search_tests.yaml (query > expected URL prefix; the nine benchmark queries plus the G2 phrases) and a test in tests/ that runs the queries against site/search.json offline. (d) Add a spellcheck over guide prose with an allowlist file. (e) Put the human-only criteria in a docs-release checklist (planning/ or a PR template) that names the owner of each guide, using the 'Edit this page' sources already tracked. Because imported guides can be changed by other repositories, run (a)-(c) on the daily build and open the existing failure issue.

unverified: I did not install any app or run any notebook on Windows, macOS or Linux. The 6-8 minute install time, the 15-minute first-analysis target and the build times are not measured. Step counts for Persona 2 (about 45 discrete actions plus two CI waits) are estimates from reading the guides, not a timed run.
Persona timings are scripted (about 1-5 s). Human 60-second findability needs real testers. My 15-20 s figure for Persona 1 is an estimate.

I did not open the Welcome notebook's own text, the Streamlit initialiser form (labconstrictor-form.streamlit.app), or GitHub Actions runs, so 'Check that it worked' texts could not be compared with the real UI.

Search tests used the built client-side index at /search.json via the theme; I did not verify whether the theme indexes front-matter tags or aliases (needed for the G2 proposal). The original preview server on 8765 was down mid-run and I restarted a plain static server on site/ (python3 -m http.server); results should be identical, since search is client-side.

The template clone at /home/user/LabConstrictor is on a feature branch; I took the Build-track document list from origin/main and from the built site/guides/*, which agree on titles. I did not diff every page against origin/main.

Mobile layout, WCAG 2.2 AA, keyboard-only use and screen-reader behaviour were not tested here (another audit dimension). The 'heading-based' completeness scan is a heuristic (regexes in acc2/heads.py, checklist.py) and may undercount guides that give the information in prose.
